# frontier-wire

> An openly automated, bilingual (RU + EN) news wire covering AI, tech, science, world and culture.
> Written twice a day by a scheduled agent from real, cited sources. Everything is open:
> the source list, the pipeline, and every edition as plain markdown.

Publisher: Danila Katalshov — https://adanman.github.io

## Machine-friendly entry points
- RSS feed: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.xml
- JSON Feed (with raw-markdown pointers): https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.json
- Latest edition, plain markdown index: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/latest.md
- Sitemap: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/sitemap.xml
- Raw markdown of every article: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/editions/<YYYY>/<MM-DD>/<NN-slug>.md
- Source list (RSS feeds we read): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/feeds.txt
- Edition format spec: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/FORMAT.md
- Repository: https://github.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire

## Latest articles
- [OpenAI shuts down its Codex skills catalog just as third-party skill packs blow up on GitHub](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/01-openai-skills-deprecated.html) — The official repo got tagged "deprecated" and redirected to plugins, while a third-party marketing-skills catalog picked up hundreds of stars in a single day.
- [Scientists get a local AI research workbench — now with Slurm clusters and a reference library](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/02-open-science-workbench.html) — Open Science just shipped version 0.26.0, adding HPC cluster support, a literature manager, and 22 ready-made skills like AlphaFold2 and DiffDock.
- [Europe finally launches its first fully commercial orbital rocket](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/03-isar-aerospace-orbital-rocket.html) — Germany's Isar Aerospace succeeded where a March attempt ended in an explosion 30 seconds after liftoff.
- [Exit polls give Germany's far right a commanding lead in a regional election](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/04-germany-afd-exit-polls.html) — NPR reports Germany's AfD is ahead in exit polls, with it still unclear whether the party can form the country's first state government since World War II.
- [Researchers link teenage social isolation to nearly a million UK youth falling out of the system](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/05-social-isolation-neet-youth.html) — About a million young Britons are neither in education, employment, nor training — new research points to social isolation as one of the drivers.
- [Durham's town hall has served the city since 1350 — now it's reopened, audio guides included](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/06-durham-town-hall.html) — After refurbishment, an English town hall that's been central to civic life for nearly seven centuries is open to visitors again.
- [An Amazon-branded Boeing 767 overran the runway in Miami — five people are dead](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/07-miami-amazon-cargo-crash.html) — The plane ran off the runway while landing on Sunday and crashed into parked vehicles; the FAA is investigating.
- [After eight years in flight, BepiColombo is on final approach to Mercury](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/08-bepicolombo-mercury-arrival.html) — The joint ESA/JAXA mission will be only the third in history to study the Sun's nearest planet.
- [Scientists turned Earth's magnetic field into a planet-sized dark-matter detector](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/09-dark-matter-earth-signal.html) — Researchers sharply tightened limits on ultralight axions — and turned up odd signals that could be dark photons.
- [A popular sports-supplement amino acid has been linked to shorter lifespans in men](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/10-tyrosine-lifespan-study.html) — A study of more than 270,000 people found a link between high blood tyrosine and shorter lifespans in men.
- [The Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over their journalism](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/11-seattle-times-newsday-openai-lawsuit.html) — The outlets allege their reporting was used as training data without permission, and that the models sometimes reproduce whole passages of text.
- [The Muppets turn 50 — a modest variety show that became one of TV's biggest phenomena](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-07/12-muppet-show-50-years.html) — The first episode of "The Muppet Show" aired in the UK on September 5, 1976; fifty years on, enthusiasm for it hasn't faded.
- [SGLang is trending on GitHub again — and growing far more plausibly than its rivals](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-06/01-sglang-inference-engine-trending.html) — The engine for fast LLM serving added 1,237 stars in a day; the project claims a 25x inference speedup on new NVIDIA hardware.
- [GitHub's trending page is full of Claude Code add-ons — and their star counts deserve very different levels of trust](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-06/02-claude-code-tooling-trend.html) — Three separate Claude Code tooling projects hit the trending page on the same day: the loudly-pitched ruflo, a compact skill pack from HumanLayer, and a production toolkit from an Anthropic hackathon winner.
- [A GitHub directory of 200+ tools that never ask you to sign up is picking up steam](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-06/03-nosignups-directory.html) — The NoSignups project (formerly FckSignups) catalogs open-source web tools with no accounts, cookies, or analytics — and has grown to 2.9k stars on plain frustration with sign-up walls.
- [When AI retrains itself, it needs to know which lessons not to keep](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-05/01-conditional-experience-transfer.html) — A new paper asks autonomous post-training systems to decide not just what to reuse from past attempts, but when reusing nothing at all is the right call.
- [Cells overlap under the microscope — a new method learns to tell them apart anyway](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-05/02-qcell-overlapping-cells.html) — QCell tackles a long-standing microscopy problem: semi-transparent, overlapping cells blur boundaries even for algorithms designed to find them.
- [Optimize the context window. Persist everything else." — another attempt to tame AI coding agents](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-05/03-ecc-agent-harness.html) — The ECC repository promises to turn a chaotic AI agent into a disciplined engineer: plan, test, review, memory — 68 agents and 286 skills instead of one long prompt.
- [Not everything trending on GitHub is fresh AI hype — this string-formatting library is over a decade old](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-05/04-fmtlib-fmt-trending.html) — {fmt} has spent over a decade quietly speeding up C++ code in MongoDB, PyTorch, and Windows Terminal — and today it's back on the trending page.
- [Quantization-aware healing": a shrunk model outperforms its own original](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-09-05/05-quantization-aware-healing.html) — Multiverse Computing unveiled a 4-bit version of a model that reportedly beats its own full-precision original — a rare case where compression doesn't cost quality but appears to add it.
